traveler: Pedro Simón del Corazón de Jesús Benoit
title: The Grid on the Grass: the Department of Engineers, La Plata, and the Signature of 1888
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the surveyor's son is born
stops.date_confidence: The year 1836 is attested by the Museo Etnográfico page of the UBA, which gives only the year and names a French father and an Argentine mother. The day 18 February circulates widely in retellings and is not corroborated by that source, so month and day default to 01. The dossier places the birth house at Bolívar 793 and Independencia in San Telmo, which geocodes to -34.6170, -58.3731, but no independent confirmation of the address was found, so the pin is the canonical Buenos Aires point already carried in this atlas.
stops.campa: A son is born to Pierre Benoit, a French surveyor and architect who came up the Plata in 1818 with his politics behind him, and to his Argentine wife. They name the boy Pedro Simón del Corazón de Jesús. The father draws for the young state, in the technical circle around its public works, at a moment when the country is still deciding its own shape on paper. The family carries a second inheritance besides the drawing board: a rumour, already old, that the father is the lost dauphin of France.
suggested_refs: The Rivadavia-era circle of French emigre engineers and architects in Buenos Aires, in which Pierre Benoit worked from 1818

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the drawing table at fourteen
stops.date_confidence: Entry to the Buenos Aires provincial Topographic Department at about age fourteen is attested by derecho.uba.ar. No primary personnel record was located, and month and day are unknown, defaulting to 01. The department's premises within the city were not identified, so the pin is the canonical Buenos Aires point rather than a documented address.
stops.campa: At about fourteen he is set to a table in the provincial Department of Topography, a meritorious draughtsman with no university behind him and none coming. What he learns he learns from the instruments: the theodolite, the chain, the field notebook ruled for angles, the convention that turns a walked boundary into a line. Eleven years pass this way. The province comes to know his hand before it knows his name, and when he finally asks to be registered as a public surveyor the board waives the examination on the strength of the service already done.
suggested_refs: The Departamento Topográfico of the province of Buenos Aires, the technical school Benoit actually attended

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Consuelo del Infortunio No. 3
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The date 26 October 1858 and the lodge name come from Masonic biographical sources cited in the dossier which were not reached directly in this pass. Benoit's Freemasonry as such is separately attested by derecho.uba.ar, though only for the later La Plata lodge of 1884. The lodge's meeting place is unknown, so the pin is the canonical Buenos Aires point.
stops.campa: He is received into the lodge Consuelo del Infortunio No. 3 on the twenty-sixth of October 1858, at twenty-two. The lodges of Buenos Aires in these years hold the men who will draw the country's maps and sign its contracts, engineers and officials and merchants of a state assembling itself, and Benoit belongs to that network for the rest of his working life. Later readers will hunt the square and the compass through everything he lays out, in a cemetery gate, in the diagonals of a city not yet imagined.
suggested_refs: Masonic biographical registers of the Gran Logia de la Argentina for Benoit's initiation and lodge affiliations
sources: pedro_benoit.dossier.md, Masonic section, citing masoneria-argentina.org.ar and symbolos.com

stops.name: Boca del Riachuelo, the first signed sheet
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The dated survey of Domingo Iglesias's property at the mouth of the Riachuelo, 20 August 1859, is listed in the dossier's works catalogue from the provincial Dirección de Geodesía archive. That archive record was not consulted directly in this pass.
stops.campa: He signs a survey of Domingo Iglesias's ground facing the mouth of the Riachuelo, dated the twentieth of August 1859, one of the earliest drawings catalogued under his own name. Measuring it is ordinary work, a boundary fixed for a private owner, and the sheet goes into the provincial archive of the Dirección de Geodesía with hundreds like it, where it is known now only by its catalogue entry. The river here is the working edge of the city: tanneries, saladeros, shallow brown water that no ocean ship can enter.
suggested_refs: The catalogued Benoit plans in the archive of the Dirección de Geodesía of the province of Buenos Aires
sources: pedro_benoit.dossier.md, works catalogue (provincial Dirección de Geodesía)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the marriage to Dolores Vázquez Silva
stops.date_confidence: The year 1860 and the bride's name are attested by derecho.uba.ar. The precise day, 14 April, and the parish of the Inmaculada Concepción come from genealogical material in the dossier that was not reached directly, and the parish coordinates are approximate. A cemetery-derived source in the dossier gives 1880 for this marriage instead; the twenty-year discrepancy is recorded and not resolved here.
stops.campa: He is twenty-four when he marries Dolores Vázquez Silva at a Buenos Aires parish, in a year the sources give as 1860 and one cemetery record gives as 1880. He has been at a drawing table in a government office since he was fourteen. Ten children will come of the marriage, and one of them, Pedro Juan, takes up his father's trade and will finish what his father leaves standing in scaffolding. The household moves out to Merlo, where the surveyor has a town to lay out, and stays there roughly twenty years at the end of a rail line.
suggested_refs: Parish registers of the Inmaculada Concepción, Buenos Aires, for the 1860 marriage record

stops.name: Buenos Aires, registered without examination
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Museo Etnográfico page of the UBA for 1861, including the exemption from the ordinary examination in recognition of eleven years of prior service, and the subsequent land-surveying work and rural bridges. Month and day unknown, defaulting to 01.
stops.campa: He is entered on the register of public surveyors of the province and begins to work for himself. The examination is waived: eleven years in the Topographic Department are counted in its place, which is to say the province certifies him against his own record instead of a syllabus. The work that follows is the plain work of a province filling in, boundaries run across camp, timber bridges thrown over creeks, subdivisions drawn for owners who want their land in rectangles. He is twenty-five and holds no diploma of any kind.
suggested_refs: The provincial register of agrimensores públicos, entry of 1861

stops.name: Merlo, a town for Juan Dillon
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The Dillon commission of 1859 and the roughly twenty years of residence in Merlo are reported in local Merlo histories relayed by the dossier; no commission document was reached. Month and day unknown. Merlo is separately confirmed by 0223.com.ar as one of the towns whose layout is credited to him, but without a date.
stops.campa: Juan Dillon, landowner and official, wants a town where his land is, and hires the young surveyor to draw one. Benoit sets out the streets, the plaza, the blocks that will be sold: the standard instrument of Argentine settlement in these decades, a grid pegged into grass ahead of the people who are going to live in it. More than ten towns in the province are credited to him, and this is the first. He moves his family into it and stays about twenty years. No commission document survives; the year 1859 comes from Merlo's own local histories.
suggested_refs: Municipal and parish histories of Merlo on the Dillon commission and the original traza
sources: pedro_benoit.dossier.md, works catalogue and local Merlo histories

stops.name: Merlo, the church of the Merced
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The neo-Gothic parish church of Nuestra Señora de la Merced at Merlo, dated 1863 and executed with the master builder Antonio Ayerbe, and the town's first school of 1860, both come from the dossier's works catalogue drawing on local and architectural histories. Neither was verified against a signed plan. Month and day unknown; coordinates approximate.
stops.campa: Four years after pegging out the streets he builds a church into them, a neo-Gothic Merced raised with the master builder Antonio Ayerbe. He has already given the town its first school. Neither building has been checked against a signed plan; both come down through Merlo's parish and municipal histories, which name him without producing the drawings. The pattern set here holds for thirty years and eight churches: the man who draws the plan comes back afterward to fill the lots he drew, plaza first, then school, then church.
suggested_refs: The parish church of Nuestra Señora de la Merced, Merlo, and the first Merlo school building

stops.name: The Riachuelo, straightening the river
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Museo Etnográfico page of the UBA, which places him on the rectification and canalization of the Riachuelo in 1863 as part of the city's port and drainage engineering. Month and day unknown, defaulting to 01. The pin is the river mouth at La Boca rather than any specific reach of the works.
stops.campa: The Riachuelo bends where it likes and silts where it likes, and Buenos Aires needs it to behave, because the only port the city has is this crooked creek. Benoit works on the rectification and the canalization, the straightening of a river into a channel. The water he measured for a private owner four years ago is now a public work. It is hydraulic engineering, and he has had no training in it; what he knows he has picked up on the job and from the instruments.
suggested_refs: The nineteenth-century rectification works of the Riachuelo and the Buenos Aires port question

stops.name: Ituzaingó, Santa Rosa laid out
stops.date_confidence: Attested: es.wikipedia's Pedro Benoit article gives 1872 for the urban plan of Santa Rosa de Ituzaingó. The commissioning landowner Manuel Rodríguez Fragio comes from the dossier and was not independently confirmed. Month and day unknown. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for Ituzaingó; a working value in the research pool sat about a kilometre away.
stops.campa: Another owner, Manuel Rodríguez Fragio, another grid. Santa Rosa de Ituzaingó goes onto paper the way Merlo did, and the province keeps filling in along the western railway. Whether Rodríguez Fragio was really the man who paid for it is asserted by later writers and confirmed by nobody. Benoit is thirty-six and has been drawing for the state, or against its background, since he was fourteen. There is no signature style to look for in this work and no argument in it: blocks, reserved lots, a plaza.
suggested_refs: The founding traza of Santa Rosa de Ituzaingó, partido de Ituzaingó

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the first sight of it
stops.date_confidence: Attested by 0223.com.ar, which reports that he first visited in 1874 and was taken with the landscape of the emerging beach resort. This is local journalism drawing on family memory; no independent confirmation was found in official heritage sources, so treat it as a locally reported tradition. Month and day unknown.
stops.campa: Four hundred kilometres south of the capital there is a saladero, a chapel, a beach, and the beginning of a resort on the Peralta Ramos family's land. Benoit comes down and looks at it. He is thirty-eight, in the middle of a provincial career, and nothing here is his commission or his work. Twenty-two years from now he will retire to this town, and twenty-three years from now he will die in it. The visit is remembered only inside the family, and reaches the record through a Mar del Plata newspaper in 2020.
suggested_refs: The Peralta Ramos settlement of Mar del Plata and its saladero origins

segments.name: The Public Buildings of the Old Capital

stops.name: Moreno 350, the Law Faculty remodelled
stops.date_confidence: The building is attested as his by the Museo Etnográfico's own page, which names the Law Faculty of the UBA among the public buildings he built but gives no year at all. derecho.uba.ar dates the plans to 1878; a working chronology in the research pool gave 1877, and the two datings are left standing side by side rather than merged. Month and day unknown. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for Moreno 350, Monserrat.
stops.campa: Dean José María Moreno wants the Faculty of Law rebuilt, and the surveyor from the country towns gets the commission. Benoit designs the remodelling and directs it. The attribution comes down to us from the institution that occupies the building now: it is the Museo Etnográfico Juan B. Ambrosetti that names him, in its own account of itself, and it gives no year for the work. The law school moved on long ago, and the rooms hold masks and textiles and human remains in cases, under a roof drawn for jurisprudence.
suggested_refs: The Museo Etnográfico Juan B. Ambrosetti, Moreno 350, in the former Faculty of Law

stops.name: The Cabildo, adapted for the courts
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1879 by the Ministry of Culture's monument record for the Cabildo de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, which names the remodelling as projected by Pedro Benoit to adapt the building as seat of the Tribunales de Justicia. That page mentions no other author. Month and day unknown, defaulting to 01. The coordinates are the corpus Cabildo pin, inherited unchanged from juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json; a Nominatim geocode of Bolívar 65 gives -34.6089, -58.3737.
stops.campa: The town hall of the colony, the building the May Revolution was declared from, is to become a courthouse. Benoit redraws its insides for the Tribunales de Justicia and sets an ornamental tower above the old arcade. The tower stands about a decade. When the city cuts the Avenida de Mayo through the block, Juan Antonio Buschiazzo, director of public works, has three arches taken off the northern side and the tower comes down with them, its weight judged a risk to the walls beneath. Nothing records what Benoit thought of that.
stops.quote: Desde 1812 en adelante sufrió modificaciones que culminaron en 1879 con la remodelación proyectada por Pedro Benoit para adaptar al Cabildo como sede de los Tribunales de Justicia.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, Ministerio de Cultura, monument record Cabildo de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires
suggested_refs: The Cabildo de Buenos Aires before the 1888-89 truncation, and the removal of Benoit's tower under Juan Antonio Buschiazzo
sources: juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json, stop 'Cabildo de Buenos Aires: three arches off the north side'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, batteries for the losing side
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. Benoit's design or supervision of defensive works and artillery batteries for the provincial side in the June 1880 fighting, and the rank of lieutenant colonel of engineers afterward, are reported in the dossier's institutional synthesis with no primary order located. The coordinates are a rough approximation of the city's southern defensive perimeter; no specific battery site was identified. The date is the month of the fighting, used to place the stop.
stops.campa: The province of Buenos Aires and the national government go to war over which of them owns the city they share. Benoit, an engineer of the province, lays out earthworks and gun positions on its southern approaches. The province loses. He is made a lieutenant colonel of engineers afterward, on the losing side. Julio Argentino Roca takes the presidency, the city is federalized, and the province wakes up a territory with no capital of its own. Every line Benoit draws for the next fifteen years follows from that defeat. No order commissioning the works has been found, and no battery site is identified.
suggested_refs: The 1880 revolution over the federalization of Buenos Aires and the provincial defensive works

stops.name: The Lomas de la Ensenada de Barragán, choosing ground
stops.date_confidence: The site and the reasons for it are attested by the Ministry of Culture's monument record for the La Plata casco urbano fundacional, which names the Lomas de la Ensenada de Barragán and the criteria of room to grow, a future overseas port, and rail and coastal connection. Benoit's individual part in locating, levelling and subdividing is corroborated there only in general terms, through the Department of Engineers. Month and day unknown. The pin is Plaza Moreno, the centre of the plan that follows, inherited from the corpus La Plata pin; the surveying itself covered open country toward Ensenada.
stops.campa: Governor Dardo Rocha and his minister Carlos D'Amico send men out to find a capital. What they settle on is high ground between Buenos Aires and the Ensenada de Barragán: room to grow in every direction, a port that can be dug later, a coast and a railway within reach. There is nothing standing on it. Benoit is a senior figure of the provincial Department of Engineers, and the official record credits the locating, the levelling and the parcelling to that department rather than to any one man. No source reached says what he himself did out on the grass.
suggested_refs: The 1881 site studies commissioned by Dardo Rocha and Carlos D'Amico for the new provincial capital

stops.name: La Plata, the plan approved and the name given
stops.date_confidence: The approval of the plan in 1882 and the naming of the city on José Hernández's suggestion are attested by the Ministry of Culture's record for the casco urbano fundacional, which credits the plan to the province's Department of Engineers and gives the cross-and-rhombus diagonal scheme to the architect Juan Martín Burgos. That record gives no day. The day 6 June is an inference of this file, not of a source: visitalaplata.com.ar reports a bronze plaque installed on the Casilla Benoit on 6 June 1948 marking the sixty-sixth anniversary of the approval of the urban plans.
stops.campa: The plan is approved: a square of streets crossed on the diagonal, a plaza every six blocks, a rhombus inside a cross inside a grid. The official record credits it to the provincial Department of Engineers as a body, gives the diagonal geometry to the architect Juan Martín Burgos, and has the surveyor Carlos Glade drawing the sheet that reaches the executive. Benoit heads the department. José Hernández, who put Martín Fierro on the pampa, proposes the name La Plata and it is taken.
suggested_refs: The 1882 approved plan of La Plata and the Burgos cross-and-rhombus scheme

stops.name: Plaza Moreno, the foundation
stops.date_confidence: Attested. 19 November 1882, at the site of Plaza Moreno, per the Ministry of Culture's record for the casco urbano fundacional and es.wikipedia's La Plata article. The same official record states that sole authorship of the design has been erroneously assigned to Benoit, so his role here is that of a directing executive, not an inventor. The coordinate is the corpus La Plata pin, carried unchanged from carlos_maria_della_paolera.journey.json; a Nominatim geocode of Plaza Moreno gives -34.9207, -57.9561.
stops.campa: On the nineteenth of November the foundation stone goes into the ground at the centre of the square, with a time capsule under it, and a province that lost its capital two years ago begins another one on grass. What follows has no real precedent in the country: cathedral, government house, legislature, port, railway, waterworks, all at once, the whole layout standing in about twenty-five months. Benoit directs a large share of it out of the Department of Engineers.
stops.quote: Surge como acción más relevante de la tarea cumplida por el ingeniero Pedro Benoit la que desarrolló como director de los trabajos de emplazamiento de la ciudad de La Plata, proyectando la ubicación de edificios públicos, parques y plazas.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, Ministerio de Cultura, monument record Sepulcro de Pedro Benoit (Decreto 2317/1983)
suggested_refs: The founding decree of La Plata, 19 November 1882
Carlos María della Paolera's unbuilt 1944 Gran Centro Cívico, proposed as an insertion into this plan
sources: carlos_maria_della_paolera.journey.json, stop 'La Plata, a civic centre for a city already drawn'

stops.name: Casa de Gobierno, the cornerstone
stops.date_confidence: Attested. es.wikipedia's Casa de Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires gives the cornerstone as 27 November 1882, construction 1883 to 1892, inauguration 1892, and Jules Dormal as directing architect. The national monument decree quoted here places the plans with the Architecture Section under Benoit. The assistance of the Italian architect Luis Baldi appears in the decree but not in the encyclopedia article, and is left flagged. Coordinates are the block bounded by calles 5, 6, 51 and 53 facing Plaza San Martín; a working value in the research pool was about 620 metres off.
stops.campa: Eight days after the foundation the stone of the Government Palace is laid. The decree that will one day make it a national monument records how the work was ordered: the executive instructs the provincial Department of Engineers to draw the plans, and the drawing falls to the Architecture Section under Benoit. Jules Dormal takes over the facades and the interiors and carries the building to its inauguration in 1892. The same decree puts an Italian architect, Luis Baldi, beside Benoit on the work; the encyclopedias name Dormal and no Baldi at all.
stops.quote: En el año 1882, el PODER EJECUTIVO dispone que el DEPARTAMENTO DE INGENIEROS PROVINCIAL, proyecte los planos del edificio, quedando esto a cargo de la Sección Arquitectura dirigida por el arquitecto Pedro BENOIT.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, national historic-monument decree text for the La Plata Government Palace (norma-304920)
suggested_refs: The Casa de Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, La Plata, and the Dormal facades

stops.name: San Ponciano, the first church of the new capital
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. San Ponciano as the city's first Catholic church, begun in the foundation period and opened in 1883, is reported in the dossier's works catalogue and is not confirmed against a signed plan. Month and day unknown, defaulting to 01. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for the Basílica de San Ponciano; a working value in the research pool was about 760 metres off and was reused for two other items in the same pool.
stops.campa: The city gets a parish before it gets most of its houses. San Ponciano opens in 1883, credited to the architecture section Benoit runs, and for a while it is the tallest thing standing on the grid. Around it sit the prefabricated cabins the province has ordered for its engineers and its clerks, wood and zinc, unloaded off ships. A church of brick among fifty huts, and the cathedral that is meant to face the great plaza is not yet out of the ground.
suggested_refs: The Basílica de San Ponciano, La Plata, first parish of the founding period

stops.name: Calles 5 y 47, the casilla from the United States
stops.date_confidence: Attested for February 1884 by visitalaplata.com.ar, which reports the arrival by ship from the United States of the first fifty prefabricated wood and zinc cabins and identifies the surviving one as the working headquarters of Benoit as chief of the Engineers Corps, a few metres from the San Ponciano church. es.wikipedia's Parque Saavedra article gives the original corner as 5 and 46 rather than 5 and 47, a one-block discrepancy left open. Day unknown within February. Coordinates are one block from San Ponciano.
stops.campa: Fifty prefabricated cabins of wood and zinc come off ships from the United States in February and go up on the empty blocks. One of them becomes the office of the chief of the Engineers Corps. Benoit works in it on the cathedral drawings and on the public works of a capital rising around him at speed. The town will later call this hut the place where the plan of the city was drawn. The plan was approved in 1882 and the hut landed in 1884. Sources disagree even about the corner it stood on, 5 and 47 or 5 and 46.
suggested_refs: The Casilla Benoit, sole survivor of the fifty prefabricated cabins of February 1884

stops.name: La Plata, the lodge Luz y Verdad No. 79
stops.date_confidence: Attested by derecho.uba.ar, which reports his membership of Freemasonry and his founding of, or part in founding, the lodge Luz y Verdad No. 79 in 1884. The dossier adds a second La Plata lodge, La Plata No. 80, in 1885, from Masonic sources not reached in this pass. Month and day unknown. The coordinates are an approximation within the new city; no meeting place was identified.
stops.campa: The men building the capital found a lodge inside it, and Benoit is among them. Engineers, officials, merchants, the people who order the bricks and sign the contracts, meeting under the square and the compass in a city that is itself all square and compass work. A century afterward the reading will run the other way: the diagonals as a Masonic figure, the cemetery gate as a temple door, the whole plan as a coded object. What the record actually holds is that he was there in 1884.
suggested_refs: The La Plata lodges Luz y Verdad No. 79 (1884) and La Plata No. 80 (1885)

stops.name: The Cathedral of La Plata, the stone that outlasts him
stops.date_confidence: Attested in part: es.wikipedia's Catedral de La Plata gives the foundation stone in 1884, names Benoit and the architect Ernesto Meyer, names Emilio Coutaret as collaborator, and dates the towers' completion to 1999. The dossier's co-attribution to the engineer Pedro Pico is not corroborated there and is left flagged rather than dropped. Month and day unknown. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode; two different and both incorrect pairs for this building circulated in the research pool.
stops.campa: Across the square from the municipality the cathedral is begun: neo-Gothic, brick, on a scale no Argentine parish had attempted, drawn under Benoit with Ernesto Meyer at the board and, by one account, Emilio Coutaret beside them. A third name, the engineer Pedro Pico, is attached to it by one source and by no other. It rises for decades and does not finish. It is open for worship long before it is complete, and its two towers stand as blunt stumps through the whole of the twentieth century, visible from every diagonal in the city.
suggested_refs: The Catedral de La Plata, foundation stone 1884, and the Meyer drawings

stops.name: The Paseo del Bosque, the arch at the gate
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The monumental entrance arch to the Bosque, attributed to Benoit's section and demolished in 1915, comes from the dossier's works catalogue and was not independently confirmed. The year 1884 is the dossier's; month and day are unknown. Coordinates are an approximation at the principal entrance of the Paseo del Bosque.
stops.campa: The plan reserves a wood on the north-eastern edge, an inheritance from the estancia that stood here before the city, and the wood is given a gate: a monumental arch at the entrance to the Paseo del Bosque, built by the architecture section. It stands about thirty years. In 1915 the city takes it down, and no photograph or drawing of it was reached in this pass; the arch is known from a works catalogue and from nothing else. Who ordered it taken down, and why, is not recorded there.
suggested_refs: The demolished entrance arch of the Paseo del Bosque, La Plata, removed 1915

stops.name: Calle 50, the house built in sixty days
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The attribution of Dardo Rocha's La Plata residence to Benoit, and the nickname Casa de los sesenta días, are consistent in the local heritage tradition relayed by the dossier and were not confirmed against any document reached in this pass. The dossier dates the work 1885 to 1886; month and day are unknown. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for the Museo y Archivo Dardo Rocha, calle 50 no. 933.
stops.campa: The governor who founded the city needs a house inside it, and the house goes up fast enough that the speed becomes its name: the house of sixty days. Benoit is credited with it, as he is credited with most things raised in La Plata in these years, and no document reached in this pass carries his signature on it. Rocha will outlive the founding by decades and outlive Benoit by more than twenty. The house ends as a museum of the founding, with the founder's own furniture standing in the rooms.
suggested_refs: The Museo y Archivo Dardo Rocha, calle 50 no. 933, La Plata

stops.name: The municipal cemetery, ground laid out for the dead
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The design of the layout and monumental entrance of the La Plata municipal cemetery, usually dated 1886 to 1887, comes from the dossier's works catalogue and was not verified. Month and day unknown. A separate and uncorroborated report has him designing the Chacarita cemetery in Buenos Aires as early as 1870; it could not be confirmed anywhere and is flagged, not adopted. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for the Cementerio de La Plata; a working value in the research pool was about 1.9 kilometres off.
stops.campa: South of the grid, past the avenue that closes it, he sets out the cemetery at fifty: axes, quarters, a monumental gate. The hygienists of the eighties want the dead outside the town and arranged in order, and the plan gives them exactly that. Symbol-hunters will later want more from it than the hygienists ever did, and read the gate and the axes as a lodge would read them. A separate report has him laying out Chacarita in Buenos Aires as early as 1870. It could not be confirmed anywhere.
suggested_refs: The Cementerio de La Plata, its axial layout and monumental portal

stops.name: La Plata, the plan of 1888 signed
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Ministry of Culture's record for the casco urbano fundacional, which states that the Plano Actualizado of 1888 was signed by the engineer Pedro Benoit and that authorship of the plan has been erroneously attributed to him on the strength of it. Month and day unknown, defaulting to 01.
stops.campa: For exhibition abroad the province needs a clean, current sheet of the city, and the head of the Department of Engineers signs it. That signature is the whole of the case. From it descends a century of textbooks, plaques and speeches naming one man as the inventor of La Plata; against it stands the record of a collective office, Burgos with the diagonals, Glade with the drawing, Benoit at the head of the department that produced both. The heritage authority now prints the correction in its own file on the city.
stops.quote: El Plano Actualizado de 1888 fue firmado por el ingeniero Pedro Benoit, a quien se ha atribuido erróneamente la autoría del mismo.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, Ministerio de Cultura, monument record La Plata, casco urbano fundacional
suggested_refs: The Plano Actualizado of 1888, signed by Benoit for exhibition abroad
Carlos María della Paolera's 1944 proposal, which treats this plan as the fixed base of the city

stops.name: Champ de Mars, the gold medal
stops.date_confidence: Attested that the urban layout of La Plata was exhibited at the 1889 Exposition Universelle in Paris and took the Gold Medal, per the Ministry of Culture's record for the casco urbano fundacional. No source reached places Benoit himself in Paris at any point in his life; the traveller here is the drawing, not the man, and the stop is entered on that footing. The date is the opening day of the exposition, used to place the stop, not the day of the award. Coordinates are the Champ de Mars pin already carried in this atlas for the 1889 exposition.
stops.campa: The sheet signed in La Plata hangs in Paris among the exhibits of the world's fair, in the year of the tower, and it takes a gold medal. A city four hundred blocks square, laid out on empty grass and standing inside about two years, is precisely the sort of object this century wanted to look at, and the jury gives it the highest award in its class. The province sends the plan across the Atlantic. It does not send the man who signed it, and nothing in the record puts him on the Champ de Mars.
suggested_refs: The Argentine section of the Exposition Universelle of 1889 and the gold medal for the La Plata layout
sources: joseph_bouvard.journey.json, stop 'Champ de Mars, the dome opposite the tower'

stops.name: Palacio Municipal, elected to the council
stops.date_confidence: Attested by 0223.com.ar for the election as municipal councillor in 1890. His alignment with the rochista current of the Partido Autonomista Nacional comes from the dossier and was not verified against council records. Month and day unknown. Coordinates are the Palacio Municipal on calle 12 between 51 and 53 per es.wikipedia; several items in the research pool used the Plaza Moreno pin for this building instead.
stops.campa: The man who ran the office that built the city is elected to the council that runs it. Eight years after the foundation the capital has an ordinary municipal politics, deficits and factions and sessions that go late, and Benoit sits in it as a councillor of the governor's party. He is fifty-four. What survives of his life from here on is municipal paperwork rather than signed plans. Whether he was in fact a rochista is asserted by later writers and was not checked against the council minutes.
suggested_refs: The authority record for Pedro Benoit in the Archivo General de la Municipalidad de La Plata

stops.name: Uribelarrea, the church of Luján
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The inauguration of the church of Nuestra Señora de Luján at Uribelarrea on 14 July 1890 and its attribution to Benoit come from local parish and architectural tradition relayed by the dossier; neither was confirmed in this pass, and the dossier itself allows that work of these years may be his son Pedro Juan's. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for Uribelarrea, partido de Cañuelas; a working value in the research pool placed the town about sixteen kilometres too far east, in open country.
stops.campa: In a railway village in the south-west of the province a small brick church is inaugurated, dedicated to the Virgin of Luján, and the attribution goes to Benoit, as attributions in this province tend to. He has a son in the same trade by now, and a name with enough weight to draw work toward it, and the local records do not always trouble to tell the two men apart. Eight churches are counted to him in all. Which eight is a question the parishes answer differently.
suggested_refs: The church of Nuestra Señora de Luján, Uribelarrea, partido de Cañuelas

stops.name: La Plata, the coat of arms approved
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The approval of the city's coat of arms on 17 April 1891, conceived by Benoit and given final drawn form by Ernesto Meyer, comes from the dossier's synthesis of the municipal ordinance record and was not verified against the ordinance itself. Coordinates are the Palacio Municipal.
stops.campa: The council approves an arms for the city: a shield conceived by Benoit and given its final drawn form by Ernesto Meyer, the same draughtsman who worked the cathedral sheets. Nine years old, the capital now holds the whole apparatus of a place, a name from a poet, a plan from a department, a cathedral in scaffolding, a cemetery, a wood, and now an emblem in ink to stamp on its paper. Benoit is fifty-five and has had a hand in every item on that list. The ordinance passes on the seventeenth of April.
suggested_refs: The municipal ordinance of 17 April 1891 approving the coat of arms of La Plata

stops.name: Palacio Municipal, the intendencia
stops.date_confidence: Attested that he took the intendencia on 18 September 1893, both by es.wikipedia and by the municipal archive's authority record quoted here. The two disagree on the end: es.wikipedia gives 15 September 1894, the archive record segments the office into three broken stretches ending 25 September 1894. The discrepancy is recorded and left standing. The municipal deficit and his defence of the founding plan come from the dossier. Coordinates are the Palacio Municipal.
stops.campa: He takes the intendencia in September 1893 and holds it, with breaks, for a year. The city is in deficit. The plan is under pressure from owners who would like the reserved blocks and the diagonals adjusted to suit them, and the intendente happens to be the man from the office that drew both. The municipal archive does not record one term but three, cut and resumed and cut again. It does not agree with the encyclopedias about when the last of them ended.
stops.quote_source: Archivo General de la Municipalidad de La Plata, authority record for Pedro Benoit
suggested_refs: The segmented service dates of Benoit's intendencia in the Archivo General de la Municipalidad de La Plata

segments.name: The Sea, and the Last Worksite

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the cornerstone at San Martín and Mitre
stops.date_confidence: Attested: es.wikipedia's Catedral de Mar del Plata confirms the cornerstone in January 1893, Benoit as architect working initially without fee, and construction from 1893 to 1905. The day 18 January comes from the dossier and was not separately confirmed. 0223.com.ar reports, on the testimony of the descendant Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit, that he charged nothing and contributed his own funds; no payment record was located, so the unpaid-work claim is reported testimony, not documentary proof. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode for Bartolomé Mitre 1780.
stops.campa: The resort town wants a cathedral, and Benoit, who has been coming here for nineteen years, takes the work for nothing. Neo-Gothic again, brick again, at the corner of San Martín and Mitre, a block back from the sea. He is fifty-six and about to become intendente of another city four hundred kilometres north, and he draws this one as a private man doing a favour to a place he likes. The governor of Buenos Aires contributes to the building; so, his family says, does Benoit, out of his own pocket. His son Pedro Juan will finish it after him.
stops.quote: A Benoit le encantaba vivir en Mar del Plata y cuando surgió que a la ciudad le hacía falta una imponente catedral, él no dudó en tomar el proyecto por el que no cobró un centavo. Incluso, si bien el gobernador de Buenos Aires contribuyó con la obra, él también puso plata de su bolsillo.
stops.quote_source: Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit, descendant, quoted in 0223.com.ar, 22 November 2020
suggested_refs: The Catedral Basílica de los Santos Pedro y Cecilia, Mar del Plata, completed by Pedro Juan Benoit

stops.name: Avenida Colón, the retirement
stops.date_confidence: Attested for late 1896 by 0223.com.ar, which reports the permanent move after retiring and a large welcome organised by Peralta Ramos. The specific house on Avenida Colón, and the earlier stay in a Peralta Ramos property, are descendant testimony in the dossier and were not verified; the coordinates are a rough approximation. The month is set to November to place the stop within the reported late 1896.
stops.campa: He gives up his Buenos Aires and La Plata work and comes down to live by the sea. Peralta Ramos, whose family owns the town, throws a party to receive him. He stays first in a Peralta Ramos property and then buys a house on Avenida Colón, and the cathedral he is building without pay is a short walk from it, which is where he goes. He has been on the provincial payroll since 1850, and he leaves the public service, by his descendants' account, in debt.
stops.quote: Fue uno de los constructores más adelantados de la época, a quien le debemos nuestra ciudad y que entró en la administración pública con dinero pero se fue con deudas.
stops.quote_source: Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit, descendant, quoted in El Día (La Plata), 8 October 2021
suggested_refs: The Peralta Ramos family and the founding of Mar del Plata as a resort

stops.name: La Plata, elected vice-dean two months before the end
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The constituent assembly of the Faculty of Physical and Mathematical Sciences of the Provincial University of La Plata electing Benoit vice-dean on 14 February 1897, alongside dean Julián Romero and delegates Jorge Coquet and Luis Monteverde, comes from the dossier's institutional chronology and was not reached directly. Popular and even some institutional retellings inflate this into a professorship and vice-deanship at the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Buenos Aires; derecho.uba.ar's fuller chronology contradicts that and records no completed teaching. Coordinates are an approximation for the early university's premises.
stops.campa: The province opens a university of its own in La Plata, and its faculty of physical and mathematical sciences constitutes itself. The assembly elects Julián Romero dean and Benoit vice-dean, with Jorge Coquet and Luis Monteverde as delegates. He never takes a class there. The minutes of that assembly were not reached in this pass. Retellings will promote this small office into a chair at the University of Buenos Aires, which he never held. The university is inaugurated publicly two months later. By then he is dead.
suggested_refs: The 1897 constituent records of the Facultad de Ciencias Físico-Matemáticas, Universidad Provincial de La Plata

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the last inspection
stops.date_confidence: Attested by 0223.com.ar, which reports that on the morning of 4 April 1897 he toured the construction site to check its progress before going home. The account is local journalism resting on family testimony transmitted by the descendant Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit; no contemporaneous eyewitness record survives.
stops.campa: On the morning of the fourth of April he walks over to the worksite to see how far the walls have come. The cathedral is four years into a construction that will take twelve. He looks at it, speaks to whoever is working, and goes home. No contemporaneous witness wrote any of that down. It comes through the family a century later, told of an old engineer inspecting a building he is partly paying for himself, two blocks from the beach he first saw twenty-three years ago.
suggested_refs: The Mar del Plata cathedral worksite at San Martín and Mitre, April 1897

stops.name: Mar del Plata, death at home
stops.date_confidence: Attested. The date 4 April 1897 is confirmed both by 0223.com.ar and by the national heritage record for his tomb, whose sentence is quoted here. The cause, cardiac insufficiency, his age of 61, and the refusal of treatment from the physician Ángel Garay are locally reported and ultimately descendant-sourced; no medical record survives to confirm them. Coordinates are the approximate Avenida Colón residence.
stops.campa: That evening he falls ill. A doctor is called, Ángel Garay, and by the family's account Benoit refuses to let himself be treated. He dies in the night of cardiac insufficiency, sixty-one years old, with this cathedral unroofed, the La Plata cathedral towerless, more than ten towns on the pampa laid out in his hand and more than eighteen hundred plans signed. There is no clinical record and no contemporaneous witness. There is a house on Avenida Colón and a date, and the state's own file gives the date and nothing else.
stops.quote: El ingeniero don Pedro Benoit falleció el 4 de abril de 1897.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, Ministerio de Cultura, monument record Sepulcro de Pedro Benoit
suggested_refs: The descendant testimony of Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit on his last night

stops.name: Recoleta, the burial
stops.date_confidence: The burial at Recoleta is attested by the national heritage record for the tomb, which confirms the location and the later designation but says nothing of the funeral. The date of about 6 April, and Dardo Rocha's oration with its declaration that Benoit's name cannot be forgotten while La Plata survives, come from commemorative literature relayed by the dossier and were not reached directly. Coordinates are the cemetery, not the located vault.
stops.campa: The body goes north to Buenos Aires and into the Recoleta, among the old families and the presidents. Dardo Rocha, governor when the city was founded and the man who signed the decree, is said to have spoken over the grave, and the tradition has him saying that Benoit's name cannot be forgotten for as long as La Plata survives. Rocha lives another quarter of a century after that sentence. Neither the oration nor the date of the funeral was found in any source reached.
suggested_refs: The Benoit vault in the Cementerio de la Recoleta, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Parque Saavedra, the hut moved and plaqued
stops.date_confidence: Attested by visitalaplata.com.ar: the businessman Carlos Servente bought the property where the casilla stood and donated it to the municipality in 1940, after which the cabin was moved to Parque Saavedra; a bronze plaque honouring Benoit was installed on it on 6 June 1948, in a ceremony with municipal officials and his descendants, marking the sixty-sixth anniversary of the approval of the urban plans. Month and day of the 1940 donation unknown. Coordinates are Parque Saavedra; a working value in the research pool was about 2.9 kilometres off, in the wrong direction.
stops.campa: The last of the fifty imported huts is bought together with the land under it, given to the city, and carried across town into a park. It is the only physical remainder of the improvised settlement the capital was built out of. In June 1948 officials and Benoit's descendants gather at it and screw a bronze plaque to the wall, for the sixty-sixth anniversary of the approval of the plans. The wood and the zinc are still standing in Parque Saavedra, in a different quarter of the city from the block they were unloaded on.
suggested_refs: The Casilla Benoit in Parque Saavedra, La Plata, and its plaque of 6 June 1948

stops.name: San Ponciano, the bust taken away at night
stops.date_confidence: Attested by El Día's 2021 feature on his legacy: the first bust of Benoit, by the artist Atilio Boveri, stood in the little square of the San Ponciano church, reduced from a full statue for reasons of budget, and was removed by municipal order in 1951 on the ground that it was not part of the paseo de los monumentos, taken away at night to a municipal store, and never seen again. Month and day unknown. The research pool gave the installation range as 1940s to 1951; the article itself does not date the installation. Coordinates are San Ponciano.
stops.campa: A bust by Atilio Boveri stands in the little square beside San Ponciano, cut down from the full statue first intended when the money ran short. It is the first monument the city puts up to the man it credits with inventing it. In 1951 the municipality decides the bust does not belong to the walk of monuments and sends men for it after dark. It goes into a municipal store shed. Nobody in La Plata has seen it since, and the family, seventy years on, still calls the removal an odd business.
stops.quote: Por cuestiones dudosas, en el '51 el Municipio decide sacarlo por considerar que no formaba parte del paseo de los monumentos. Se sacó de noche, algo extraño, descansó en un depósito municipal y no se sabe qué pasó.
stops.quote_source: Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit, descendant, quoted in El Día (La Plata), 8 October 2021
suggested_refs: The lost Atilio Boveri bust of Pedro Benoit, removed from the San Ponciano plazoleta in 1951

stops.name: Calles 12 y 64, the second bust
stops.date_confidence: Attested for the 1970s by El Día's 2021 feature: a second bust, by the sculptor Máximo Maldonado, was placed at the corner of calles 12 and 64, later vandalised, removed for restoration and never returned to public display. The article gives no exact year, so 1975 is a placeholder within the decade. Coordinates are the corner at the edge of Parque Saavedra; a working value in the research pool placed it about 1.7 kilometres away in the city centre.
stops.campa: A second bust, by Máximo Maldonado, goes up at a corner on the edge of Parque Saavedra, a short walk from the hut. It is attacked, taken down for restoration, and never put back. Two commissioned portraits of the man credited with the city, one lost from a municipal store and one lost in a workshop. The busts that survive are all indoors: in the cathedral, in the Rocha museum, in the intendente's own office. The obelisk on Plaza San Martín is dedicated to whoever took part in the founding, and names nobody.
stops.quote: Benoit es un ejemplo de honradez, aunque su nombre no se encuentra entre los grandes próceres nacionales, toda vez que su valía, prestigio y mérito individual no configuran el estereotipo que la historia solo reserva para aquellos héroes de proezas bélicas. Se le deben las ciudades más pujantes de Buenos Aires, pero sin embargo se encuentra deambulando en el ostracismo revisionista.
stops.quote_source: Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit, descendant, quoted in El Día (La Plata), 8 October 2021
suggested_refs: The Máximo Maldonado bust of Benoit at calles 12 and 64, removed for restoration and not reinstalled

stops.name: Recoleta, the tomb declared national
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Ministry of Culture's record for the tomb: it holds the designation of National Historic Sepulchre, declared a national monument by Decree 2317 of 1983. The month and day of the decree were not given on the page reached, so they default to 01. The page does not describe the tomb's design.
stops.campa: Eighty-six years after the funeral the national government declares the vault a historic sepulchre by decree. The text that accompanies the designation is short. It calls him the director of the works of emplacement of the city, not its author, and it gives the intendencia and the cathedral one flat sentence each, with no adjectives at all. The month and the day of the decree are not on the page that carries it; only the year, 1983. Nor does the page say anything about the tomb itself, who built it or what it looks like.
stops.quote: El ingeniero Pedro Benoit fue en 1893 intendente municipal de La Plata y contribuyó a la construcción de la Catedral de aquella ciudad.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, Ministerio de Cultura, monument record Sepulcro de Pedro Benoit
suggested_refs: Decree 2317/1983 declaring the Benoit sepulchre a national historic monument

stops.name: La Plata, the cathedral towers finished
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia's Catedral de La Plata: the completion contract for the two 112-metre towers was awarded on 16 February 1998 to a temporary association of the firms Carner and Palma-Rol Ingeniería, under the provincial administration of Eduardo Duhalde, and the work, including twenty-five bells and the ornamental pinnacles, was finished at the end of 1999. The month is set to December to place the stop at the end of that year.
stops.campa: The two towers go up at last, a hundred and twelve metres each, with twenty-five bells and the stone pinnacles the original drawings called for. The contract goes out in February 1998, to Carner and Palma-Rol Ingeniería under the provincial administration of Eduardo Duhalde, and the work is done by the end of the following year. A hundred and fifteen years have passed since the foundation stone went into the ground. Argentines who grew up with a flat-topped cathedral do not recognise the skyline afterward.
suggested_refs: The 1998-1999 completion works on the towers of the Catedral de La Plata

stops.name: La Plata, the council names Burgos
stops.date_confidence: Attested by El Día's 2017 investigation: in 2000 the engineer Antonio Enrique Corrado petitioned the city council to recognise the architect Juan Martín Burgos's part in the design, and the council responded with an ordinance recognising Burgos as an inspirer of the urban plan. The same article traces the revision back to research published in the 1950s by Professor José María Rey; a working chronology in the research pool gave the bare year 1950, which is more precise than the source allows. Month and day of the ordinance unknown.
stops.campa: A hundred and eighteen years after the founding, on the petition of an engineer named Antonio Enrique Corrado, the council of La Plata passes an ordinance naming Juan Martín Burgos an inspirer of the plan of the city. Behind that ordinance lie fifty years of archival work, beginning with José María Rey in the 1950s and carried on by the architectural historian Alberto de Paula, whose conclusion is flat and unhedged. Benoit's descendants dispute it in the newspapers, and go on disputing it.
stops.quote: De manera que de ahí en más, sigue la atribución a Benoit, sobre la autoría del plano de La Plata, pero no es el autor.
stops.quote_source: Alberto S. J. de Paula, architect and historian, quoted in El Día (La Plata), 26 March 2017
suggested_refs: The year-2000 La Plata municipal ordinance recognising Juan Martín Burgos, and the research of José María Rey

stops.name: La Plata, the dauphin in the family
stops.date_confidence: Attested that the claim is current: El Día published it on 18 November 2024, quoting the descendant Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit and the historian Nicolás Colombo, who points to DNA work at Louvain and Münster around the year 2000 comparing hair attributed to Marie Antoinette with heart tissue from the child who died in the Temple prison, taken as confirming that the Temple child was the authentic Louis XVII. The legend about Pierre Benoit is a family tradition and not a documented fact, and the genetic finding runs against it. Coordinates are the corpus La Plata pin.
stops.campa: The other inheritance surfaces again. Pierre Benoit, the French engineer who came up the river in 1818, was said in his own lifetime to be Louis XVII, the dauphin smuggled out of the Temple prison, and his descendants have never let the story go. In 2024 a La Plata newspaper prints it once more under a headline calling the maker of the city's plan a grandson of Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette. The DNA work at Louvain and Münster, comparing hair attributed to Marie Antoinette with tissue from the heart of the child who died in the Temple, says the child in the Temple was the dauphin.
stops.quote: Considero que existen indicios para llegar a esa conclusión. A pesar de que para el gobierno francés es un caso cerrado yo no lo veo así.
stops.quote_source: Alejandro Zuccarelli Benoit, descendant, quoted in El Día (La Plata), 18 November 2024
suggested_refs: The Pierre Benoit / Louis XVII survival legend and the Louvain and Münster DNA studies of the Temple heart
